## Evidence-size forensic addendum — 2026-11-13 (measured from current main)

This is a path-level audit supplement to WP1/WP6/WP9 and acceptance items R02/R04/R10/R20/R22. It is not permission for blind mass deletion. It records concrete, measured cleanup targets and defines a smaller evidence format that preserves reproducibility.

### 1) Current image inventory — exact tree counts

At HEAD `9d6a29d63420ad4c648a3442e543256b3c4d1dc3`:

| Scope / format | Tracked paths | Path-summed size | Unique blobs / size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| All repository images | 2,402 | 99.83 MiB | 984 / about 78.31 MiB |
| PNG (whole repo) | 1,700 | 84.46 MiB | 622 / 67.82 MiB |
| JPG/JPEG (whole repo) | 671 | 9.78 MiB | 335 / 7.05 MiB |
| GIF (whole repo) | 28 | 5.59 MiB | 24 / 3.44 MiB |
| WebP (whole repo) | 3 | negligible | 3 |
| `evidence/` images | 1,482 | 79.70 MiB | 437 / 65.17 MiB |
| `docs/evidence/` images | 636 | 16.02 MiB | 331 / 9.80 MiB |

Important distinction: these are tracked-path sizes, not Git pack/checkout measurements. Git stores one object for identical blobs, but each duplicate path is materialized in a checkout. The evidence tree contains many identical screenshot paths; deduplicating paths reduces checkout clutter/size, while it does not save the same number of Git object bytes if the blob remains reachable elsewhere.

The full `evidence/` tree is 7,264 files / 161.81 MiB path-summed; unique blobs total about 138.57 MiB, so repeated content contributes about 23.24 MiB of repeated path bytes before other cleanup.

### 2) Direct target: W14 Halma folder

Path: `evidence/s188_w14/runs/app.halma/`

| File | Actual Git tree size |
|---|---:|
| `screenshot.png` | 2,865,516 bytes (2.733 MiB) |
| `trace_summary.json` | 20,852 bytes |
| `trace.jsonl` | 11,824 bytes |
| `report.md` | 2,036 bytes |
| `lifecycle_trace.json` | 940 bytes |
| **Folder total** | **2,901,168 bytes (2.767 MiB)** |

The PNG is about 98.8% of this folder's bytes. The report states 1080×1920 and duplicates the same “Output Frame” section twice, pointing to the same screenshot. It also reports a screenshot size of **7.91 MB**, which does not match the tracked blob size of 2,865,516 bytes. Fix the report generator to read the actual file size and emit one screenshot section only.

The report's headline `SUCCESS` is not sufficient evidence of actual app behavior: it lists `APIs Called = 0`, `Frames Rendered = 2`, `Execution Time = 0ms`, and `Memory Peak = 0.00 B`. The companion trace must be read as the source of truth, not this headline.

### 3) W18 is the clearest high-volume example

Path: `evidence/s188_w18/runs/`

- 118 files in 71 subdirectories; total **30.605 MiB**.
- 11 Halma screenshots, each **2,863,792–2,863,835 bytes** (about 2.731 MiB), together about **30.04 MiB**.
- These 11 screenshots have different SHA values, so they are not exact byte duplicates. Do not call them duplicates solely by filename or near-equal file size.
- The remaining reports/traces are mostly around 1–21 KB each.

Concrete run folders:
`halma_w18_r1` … `halma_w18_r11` (11 runs). Every folder holds a full-sized 1080×1920 PNG although the reports and core trace metrics are substantially the same.

**The current evidence is internally inconsistent and must be corrected before any run is advertised as visually successful:**

- Example `halma_w18_r1/trace_summary.json`: `app_draw_ops=0`, `nodes_visited=1`, while its `frame_analysis.verdict` says `REAL_APP_CONTENT`.
- Its `trace.jsonl` has `RENDER_OK` with result `NO_APP_OPS` and state `app_ops=0`.
- The same trace records **one uncaught in-flight exception** and a stub-bounded call census (e.g. 924 IMPLEMENTED / 63 STUBBED, or 920 / 39 in another run). “Execution completed successfully” therefore needs its explicit F-016/stub caveats; it is not a clean complete-app pass.
- `halma_w18_r4/report.md` points to the APK under `store_halma_w18_r1`, not a run-specific r4 store. The report also claims 7.91 MB while the actual tracked screenshot is 2,863,825 bytes.
- The trace summary claims 975,949 app-owned pixels and a `REAL_APP_CONTENT` verdict while the correlated render trace says `NO_APP_OPS`; reconcile the ownership classifier/producer and consumer before accepting the image as genuine app UI.

This batch may still prove APK loading, manifest/DEX parse, lifecycle dispatch, surface creation, and a repeatable first-frame boundary. It does **not** prove Halma gameplay or meaningful Compose content. Retain this distinction in registries and reports.

Related high-volume wave folders (path-summed):
| Area | Total | Images |
|---|---:|---:|
| `evidence/s195_audit/` | 33.63 MiB | 6.83 MiB |
| `evidence/s188_w18/` | 31.49 MiB | 30.48 MiB |
| `evidence/s200/` | 17.27 MiB | 4.34 MiB |
| `evidence/s188_w13/` | 4.65 MiB | 3.19 MiB |
| `evidence/s188_w15/` | 3.18 MiB | 2.92 MiB |
| `evidence/s188_w14/` | 2.98 MiB | 2.84 MiB |
| `evidence/s107_games/` | 4.39 MiB | 3.10 MiB (about 2.69 MiB of repeated image path bytes) |

The 17 largest PNGs in the repository are each over 2 MiB; the top two are 3.205 MiB, and 15 others are roughly 2.73 MiB. Review all of them, not only Halma.

### 4) Exact duplicate evidence already found

Examples where identical SHA proves duplicate bytes (unlike the 11 W18 PNGs):

- `evidence/s195_audit/comments_raw.json` and `comments_raw.partial.json`: same SHA `386eb21b1f1e47ec3cc61ccd91fd79d5120e4c9d`, 7,692,786 bytes each. Keep one canonical copy and update links/manifest; remove the duplicate path.
- `evidence/s107_games/` contains many per-title run screenshots repeated byte-for-byte between run1/run2 and other audit copies. Its image path bytes are about 3.10 MiB but repeated paths account for about 2.69 MiB. Preserve one blob per unique SHA plus an index mapping every run to that SHA; do not preserve 5 identical files.
- `evidence/audit_s107/three_run/` and `evidence/s107_games/` repeat the same Hot Death screenshot SHA across several run folders.
- `evidence/s215/runs/ar_probe/screenshot.png` and `ar_probe_x2/screenshot.png` are the same SHA `d33ee378...`.
- `evidence/s108_telegram/reference_forkgram.png` and `evidence/s110_tickets/telegram/reference_forkgram_login.png` are the same SHA `2aaee215...`.
- `evidence/cont65/capaudit_face.png`, `capaudit_face_fix359.png`, and `evidence/cont67/capaudit_face.png` are byte-identical.
- `evidence/cont11/census_v2_pre_rc.json` and `census_v2_after.json` are byte-identical.

Run the complete SHA duplicate scan and produce a manifest; these examples are only a subset. Keep a single canonical object/path per identical artifact, and retain a small mapping that explains which run/claim used it.

### 5) Required artifact-retention policy — implement this, not “compress everything”

Classify every screenshot/trace into one of these tiers:

**A. Canonical golden / exact pixel evidence**
- Keep the original pixel-exact PNG or a losslessly optimized PNG.
- Lossless optimization is allowed only after pixel equality is verified (decode both images and compare every pixel; preserve dimensions/color mode/alpha).
- Update SHA256SUMS and all evidence manifests to the new byte SHA after a lossless rewrite.
- Never replace a golden with lossy JPEG/WebP.

**B. Repeated-run determinism evidence**
- Keep one representative full-resolution screenshot for the batch.
- For every other run retain a compact row: run ID, APK SHA, engine commit/binary SHA, command/config, exit status, wall time, frame count, screenshot SHA-256, pixel-diff/state metrics, exception/stub counters, and verdict.
- The SHA row must prove that every run was captured; a second full PNG is unnecessary when it adds no independent visual finding.
- Retain extra full screenshots only for a materially different frame, first divergence, regression, or state transition that the representative does not show.
- If runs are byte-identical, deduplicate to one file and map all run IDs to that file. If they differ, determine whether the differences are meaningful pixels or nondeterministic metadata/noise before deciding what to keep.

**C. Debug/triage image with no independent visual value**
- If the frame is blank/default/background-only or is not needed for pixel-exact proof, keep at most one representative thumbnail (e.g. max dimension 480–640 px, WebP quality around 75–82 or JPEG quality around 80–85) OR keep only machine-readable pixel/trace metrics where a picture adds no value.
- The preview must be explicitly labeled `DERIVATIVE / NOT PIXEL-EXACT`, with source path + source SHA + dimensions + encoder settings in a small manifest.
- Do not call a compressed preview a canonical screenshot or a new proof of behavior.

**D. Raw logs / trace detail**
- Never store multiple copies of the same report section or embed the same screenshot twice in one Markdown report.
- Promote decision-relevant trace facts to a compact summary (first divergence, app-owned draw count, ViewTree counts, state-change pixels, stub/exception census, run identity).
- Keep full raw traces only where they are needed to reproduce a disputed root cause or are referenced by a live issue. Otherwise retain a compressed diagnostic bundle outside the operational Git tree with SHA + retrieval instructions, or discard after a compact canonical summary is independently validated.
- Local stores/databases, WAL/SHM/LOCK files, extracted APK content and transient output trees must not become permanent evidence merely because they sit under a run folder.

### 6) Batch rules for W18 Halma (explicit requested action)

For the 11 `halma_w18_rN` directories:

1. Compare all 11 screenshot pixels, dimensions, alpha/channel mode, and per-image SHA; compare report/summary metrics and trace event sequences. The SHA values already show they are not byte-identical, so perform a visual/pixel-diff analysis and identify why.
2. Determine whether any run contains a distinct error, first-divergence, output, or state transition. The current reports show essentially the same status/metrics; the trace inconsistency above is a blocker.
3. Keep one representative full-size PNG for forensic reference plus one compact table/JSON summary for all 11 runs. Keep additional full images only for a demonstrated unique visual difference.
4. If the remaining screenshots are only visually equivalent default frames, delete their tracked PNG paths after recording source SHA and run mapping; do not archive 10 multi-megabyte PNGs inside Git under a different folder.
5. Correct every `report.md`: actual APK path for that run, actual screenshot byte size, one screenshot block, real elapsed time, explicit uncaught/stub counts, and a truthful verdict.
6. If an image is kept only for human review, create a small preview derivative; do not use it in pixel-exact tests.

**Expected target for this one batch:** reduce about 30.04 MiB of W18 full-size screenshots to at most one full PNG (~2.73 MiB) plus one small preview if useful, while preserving all 11 run identities, hashes, trace facts, and any genuinely different failure evidence. This is a target, not a deletion quota: if pixel analysis proves an additional run is materially different, retain it and explain why.

### 7) Future prevention — enforce the size/noise policy in the runner

Update the capture/report tooling so it does not reintroduce this problem:

- Default run artifacts should be compact: one `report.md`, one `summary.json`, one trace summary, and one screenshot only when it provides independent evidence.
- For repeated runs, write one batch-level `runs.jsonl`/TSV containing per-run metrics and SHA rather than copying the same 2.7 MB PNG into every run directory.
- Default screenshot cap for *non-canonical diagnostic previews*: max dimension 640 px and a configured byte budget (e.g. 150–250 KB). Preserve full resolution only behind an explicit `--retain-full-screenshot` or canonical-evidence opt-in.
- A canonical golden or any image used by a pixel-exact gate is exempt from lossy conversion, but must be losslessly optimized and have exact SHA/pixel checks.
- Add a pre-commit/CI evidence-size gate: warn above 500 KB; fail above 1 MiB unless a per-file allowlist entry states the evidence purpose, owner, source SHA/provenance, linked issue/test, and review/expiry condition.
- Detect byte-identical files by SHA and fail/warn on new duplicates unless a documented reason exists.
- Reject stale report sizes, duplicate screenshot embeds, missing run IDs, mismatched APK/data-root paths, `SUCCESS` when `NO_APP_OPS`/uncaught/stub-bounded semantics contradict the claim, and any mismatch between frame verdict and draw/ViewTree provenance.
- Ensure all scripts use repository-relative paths, not `/home/z/my-project` absolute paths.

### Required deliverables added to R02/R04/R10/R20/R22

- `evidence_size_inventory.tsv`: every image with path, type, byte size, dimensions, SHA, evidence class, canonical reference/consumer, and disposition.
- `evidence_duplicate_groups.tsv`: exact SHA groups, retained path, removed paths, checkout bytes avoided, and all run IDs/claims redirected to the retained path.
- `evidence_retention_manifest.json` (compact): original SHA, optional derivative SHA, lossless/lossy status, encoder/settings, pixel-equality verdict, source run and retention reason.
- `evidence_batch_summary.json` or JSONL for repeated-run output; no one-image-per-run policy by default.
- Tests proving canonical golden PNG pixels remain exact, derivatives are explicitly noncanonical, duplicate files are detected, per-run IDs/hashes survive compaction, and a deliberately contradictory `NO_APP_OPS + REAL_APP_CONTENT` report is rejected.

**Do not close the evidence-cleanup part of this issue** until the W18 11-run analysis is complete, all large images have a KEEP/OPTIMIZE/THUMBNAIL/DELETE decision, and a fresh scan proves the new runner/CI guard prevents recurrence. Preserve the no-false-success rule: compression/deletion must never erase the only evidence of a real failure or make an incomplete app appear successful.

## WP10 — Constitution-level repository layout & artifact ownership law (permanent; 2026-11-13)

**This is a permanent rule change, not just another cleanup wave.** The present disorder exists because every campaign/coder can create a plausible new folder, copy a dependency or dump output into Git without a single enforced ownership map. A one-time cleanup will regress unless the repository constitution and CI prevent it.

### A. What the two questioned directories actually contain — current-main measurement

Baseline HEAD remains `9d6a29d63420ad4c648a3442e543256b3c4d1dc3`.

#### 1. `third_party/osmesa/` — 39 file paths, 94.392 MiB

The directory is not 94 MiB of different libraries. Its composition is:

| Subtree | Paths | Path bytes |
|---|---:|---:|
| `devpkg/` | 25 | 46.279 MiB |
| `usr/` | 9 | 44.928 MiB |
| directory root | 5 | 3.184 MiB |
| **Total** | **39** | **94.392 MiB** |

Six separate tracked file paths contain the exact same 15,693,864-byte blob (SHA `75dd953d0b73e4024f597888312262af020ac0b9`):

```text
devpkg/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libOSMesa.so.6
devpkg/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libOSMesa.so.8
devpkg/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libOSMesa.so.8.0.0
usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libOSMesa.so.6
usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libOSMesa.so.8
usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libOSMesa.so.8.0.0
```

These are **six regular Git paths with identical file contents**, not six distinct library builds. Removing five paths would reduce the checkout's materialized paths by about **74.834 MiB** if one is retained. It does not automatically save 74.834 MiB of Git pack storage while one reachable blob remains; state savings honestly.

Other contents:
- Debian packages: `libosmesa6_25.0.7-2+deb13u1_amd64.deb` (3,197,344 bytes), `libosmesa6-dev_...` (23,124 bytes), `libgl-dev_...` (100,680 bytes).
- Development headers: `gl.h`, `glcorearb.h`, `glext.h`, `osmesa.h`, `khrplatform.h`.
- The extracted runtime and dev package trees duplicate parts of the .deb distributions, including docs, copyright and support files.
- `third_party/osmesa/test_osmesa.c` is a small standalone test. It calls `OSMesaCreateContextAttribs`, `OSMesaMakeCurrent`, `glGetString`, `glClear`, and `glReadPixels`, checks a pixel, and prints `OSMESA REAL GL OK`. A prebuilt `test_osmesa` executable is also tracked.

**What OSMesa is for:** Mesa's off-screen software OpenGL interface can create a software GL context and render into a memory buffer without opening a window or requiring a display server. That makes it potentially useful as a headless graphics oracle/test backend. It is conceptually different from PortableGL and from MiniAndroid's own GLES bridge/software-renderer implementation.

**What the repository proves today:** the current `miniandroid/Makefile` and `miniandroid/CMakeLists.txt` contain no OSMesa reference. The explicit OSMesa consumer visible in this subtree is the standalone sanity test. Do not advertise OSMesa as a runtime dependency unless a whole-repository symbol/include/link search proves a current runtime consumer.

**Required disposition:**
1. Search every tracked source/build/test/script/workflow/config for `OSMesa`, `osmesa`, `-lOSMesa`, `pkg-config osmesa`, dlopen paths and copied library paths. Attach the complete path/line result. Do not rely only on Makefile/CMake.
2. Determine whether this probe is still a useful independent rendering oracle for the current GLES bridge/software renderer. If yes, retain the small test source + a documented optional test recipe in a canonical location such as `tests/graphics/backends/osmesa/`; keep it opt-in and outside the runtime's required build.
3. Reproduce it in a clean Debian 13 environment from a package-manager/bootstrap route pinned to exact package version, repository source, license and SHA. A clean test must prove context creation + pixel readback.
4. **Default recommendation:** do not vendor six copies of the 15.7 MB library and a full duplicate Debian package tree in the main source checkout. Prefer the source test + pinned dependency manifest + optional installer/bootstrap. If the project requires a vendored prebuilt, retain exactly one binary whose embedded SONAME is verified by `readelf -d`, with real symlink aliases only where required; do not copy the same ELF under fake `.so.6`, `.so.8`, `.so.8.0.0` names.
5. Choose one distribution representation: either package files or one extracted, minimal runtime/development tree — never both complete trees plus .deb archives without an actual consumer.
6. If the current renderer tests no longer use OSMesa and it adds no unique differential/oracle coverage, retire the whole vendored bundle after proving that fact; preserve only any still-useful test source, recipe and historical finding.

**Do not delete OSMesa before the above test/consumer proof.** The likely end state is an optional graphics test dependency, not a runtime dependency.

#### 2. `forensic_data/` — raw GitHub audit input, not runtime source

Measured contents: **237 files / 10.883 MiB**:
- 232 JSON files = about 8.304 MiB.
- 2 gzip files = about 2.508 MiB.
- 3 patch/diff files = about 0.072 MiB.

Breakdown:
| Location | Files | Size | Meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| root of `forensic_data/` | 15 | 9.122 MiB | raw issue/comment/commit API snapshots and stats |
| `batch367/` | 219 | 1.690 MiB | per-issue and per-comment snapshots plus reconstructed records/evidence maps |
| `ar5_patch/` | 3 | 0.072 MiB | three saved patch/diff parts, not generic raw exports |

Largest raw inputs include:
- `issues_all.json` — 4,908,274 bytes, broad issue snapshot.
- `all_issue_comments.json.gz` — 2,018,897 bytes, compressed comment snapshot.
- `issue_364_comments.json` — 1,237,123 bytes.
- `s220_issues.json` — 748,505 bytes.
- `commits.json.gz` — 610,727 bytes.
- `batch367/records_final.json` — 239,565 bytes.
- `batch367/issue_8_comments.json` — 236,434 bytes.
- `batch367/evidence_map_raw.json` and `evidence_map_full.json` — about 100 KB each.

These files were used as **research/forensic source snapshots** for historical GitHub issue/comment/commit reconciliation, request reconstruction and evidence mapping. They are not APK runtime data, test fixtures or dependencies.

The repository already contains the normalized 390-record output:
- `docs/FORENSIC_ALL_REQUESTS_LEDGER.jsonl` — **390 rows / 261,416 bytes**, one normalized request row each, with issue, source/date, claimed vs verified status, evidence level, commits, refs and explanatory notes.
- `forensic_data/ledger_stats.json` — summary statistics.
- `scripts/forensic_ledger.py` — generator, whose current input contract explicitly reads `forensic_data/issues_all.json`, `all_issue_comments`, `commits.json`, then emits the normalized ledger and stats.

That means raw snapshots are inputs to a historical generator, while the compact JSONL is the useful canonical result. Do not delete inputs until the generator is migrated and the output reproduces.

**Required disposition:**
1. Inspect the 3 `ar5_patch/part*.diff` patches individually. Find their originating issue/commit, determine whether each patch was merged, superseded, or remains unmerged. A patch containing unique source changes must not be discarded just because it is small; any still-live patch belongs in a properly named patch review/provenance record, not mixed into raw API dumps.
2. Promote any remaining unique facts from `batch367/` and the root snapshots into the canonical 390-row ledger or a concise cited audit report. Add a source URL, snapshot date, source SHA and retrieval command to each retained forensic claim.
3. Change `scripts/forensic_ledger.py` so the normal source checkout does not require multi-megabyte raw API exports. It should validate/rebuild the canonical ledger from either (a) a compact checked-in, versioned normalized source, or (b) an explicitly invoked online acquisition mode that writes raw data only into an ignored `.cache/forensics/<snapshot-id>/` location. Default test/CI must not call GitHub network APIs or require secrets.
4. After a clean test proves the normalized ledger is complete and reproducible, remove raw API dumps from the normal source tree. If exact raw historical snapshots are genuinely required for audit, store them outside the working source tree (e.g. a versioned external archival asset) with a durable URL, SHA-256, retrieval script, date and retention owner. Do not simply move 10 MB of noise to another tracked folder.
5. Preserve issue links and the normalized historical audit results. Raw snapshots are not allowed to become a second canonical issue tracker or a hand-maintained shadow of current GitHub state.

# WP11 — Enforce one repository constitution for every coder and every future wave

## 1. One authority, not many informal folder conventions

Update `CONSTITUTION_V2.md` with a permanent, clearly titled chapter:

**REPOSITORY LAYOUT, DIRECTORY OWNERSHIP & ARTIFACT LIFECYCLE LAW**

Link it from `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/REPOSITORY_STRUCTURE.md`, `docs/REPOSITORY_HYGIENE.md`, and agent/coder request templates. The Constitution is the normative authority; supporting documents are explanatory/generated maps, not competing policies.

If `docs/ARTIFACT_LIFECYCLE.md` or `docs/REPOSITORY_HYGIENE.md` conflicts with the new Constitution chapter, reconcile it in the same PR. Do not create a third policy file with overlapping wording.

## 2. Allowed ownership map — every top-level path must have one clear job

Adopt and document one canonical map. Adjust names only when the migration has verified all consumers; do not rename directories gratuitously.

| Path | Sole ownership / allowed content |
|---|---|
| `miniandroid/` | Runtime implementation, required framework data, build files and maintained runtime tests; no run output |
| `tests/` | Maintained test harnesses and backend/contract tests; no one-off wave dumps |
| `fixtures/` | Small intentional source/input fixtures referenced by tests; never generated fixture build output |
| `examples/`, `games/` | First-party runnable example/game source only; define whether games is retained separately or moved into examples |
| `third_party/` | Only currently consumed vendored dependencies, or explicitly documented optional test dependencies; pinned version/license/URL/SHA/build consumer for each |
| `upstream/` | Pinned third-party source trees consumed by reproducible source-first app builds; not arbitrary reference snapshots or extracted downloads |
| `reference/` | Do not leave as a vague catch-all; either move versioned reference snapshots under one canonical documented reference area or retire it after reference provenance is reconciled |
| `canonical/` | Canonical machine-readable registries only; one owner per data family; generated projections identify their source and must never be hand-edited |
| `registry/` | Merge into `canonical/` or document a distinct non-overlapping registry contract; no second copy of the same registry |
| `docs/` | Human documentation, architecture, development guides, compatibility, decisions, releases, and navigational indexes |
| `docs/evidence/canonical/` | Small, curated proof assets referenced by canonical evidence registry; never raw run folders |
| `evidence/` | Transitional/historical campaign evidence only while migrated; no new unreviewed wave dumps; converge to one canonical evidence home |
| `scripts/` | Maintained, repeatable build/test/release/audit scripts; one-off run outputs never written beside scripts |
| `tools/` | Maintained developer tools and small required pinned tools; no scratch binaries/builds/download caches |
| `library_ecosystem/` | If retained, metadata-only dependency capability/consumer/lock registry; explicitly document its distinct role or merge into canonical dependency registry |
| `.github/` | Workflows, templates, repository automation and policy enforcement |
| `.agent/` | Short, current agent contract and pointers to Constitution; no duplicate sprawling worklog/old campaign state |
| `reports/`, `research/`, `audit/`, `forensic_data/`, `probe_store/`, `hc_provenance/`, `campaigns/` | No automatic permission to store files. Inventory and assign each to one owner above; raw/temporary exports stay outside Git. Retain a root only if its distinct role is documented and tested. |

Do not create a new root folder for each coder, session, S-wave, issue, app, run, experiment or campaign.

## 3. Root-level file law

The repository root is for a small, explicit allowlist only: README, LICENSE, Constitution, contributing/security docs, version-control/build entrypoints (Makefile/CMakeLists where intentionally needed), project metadata, and the documented top-level navigation files.

The following must not appear at the root:
- `s203_out*.txt`, `*_gate_out.txt`, raw logs, stderr/stdout captures, traces, screenshots, random JSON/JSONL, database/WAL/SHM/LOCK files;
- one-off issue reports, patches, worklogs, generated registry copies or source files that belong to a component/reference area;
- duplicate root registry copies when a canonical registry already exists.

Every root-level exception must appear in a machine-readable root allowlist with owner, purpose and expiry/review trigger.

## 4. New file / new directory creation contract — mandatory BEFORE writing

Every coder/agent/tool must do this before creating a tracked path:

1. Identify artifact class: runtime source / test / fixture / vendored dependency / reference source / canonical registry / canonical evidence / human documentation / generated output / raw log / cache / temporary scratch.
2. Find the existing canonical owner directory and registry. Reuse it; do not create a new folder because a wave name is convenient.
3. State the consumer: exact build target, test, script, documented claim or evidence ID that uses the path. If no consumer or reproducible purpose exists, do not commit the file.
4. State provenance: source URL/revision/license for third-party material; exact producing commit/tool/command for generated material; APK SHA/session/run ID for app evidence.
5. State lifecycle: KEEP / REGENERATE / EXTERNALIZE / DELETE after use; expected size; whether it is needed in a clean clone.
6. If a new top-level directory is truly necessary, first update the Constitution's ownership map, structure document, root allowlist test and issue/PR rationale in the same reviewed change. No silent directory creation.
7. A coder cannot mark an artifact as evidence merely by writing it into `evidence/`; the evidence validator must confirm that it supports a claim.

## 5. Default output routing — no new noise

- Build products, binaries, extracted APKs, package data, databases/WAL/SHM, run screenshots, raw traces, temporary JSON and debug logs go under an ignored local `.cache/`, `build/`, or explicitly configured output directory.
- Committed scripts must default to ignored output and must not write into source, docs, root or canonical evidence without an explicit promotion step.
- A run becomes permanent evidence only after a separate `promote-evidence` step creates a compact summary, validates provenance and selects only necessary assets.
- Raw GitHub/API research exports must use ignored `.cache/forensics/`; commit distilled findings and source links, not unbounded API dumps.
- A test run should never leave new tracked files when executed from a clean checkout.
- Historical campaign artifacts may remain temporarily during the migration, but no new wave should add to an unowned legacy area.

## 6. Automated enforcement — Constitution must be executable

Implement a dependency-free policy validator invoked by CI and a local preflight:

- Exact allowed top-level files/directories list; unknown new root entries fail with a clear instruction.
- Directory ownership map and artifact class per new tracked path.
- Reject APK/AAB, extracted app trees, build/cache/temp outputs, raw stdout/stderr/logs, DB/WAL/SHM/LOCK, Python bytecode, unapproved ELF/archive binaries and scratch traces.
- Reject newly introduced screenshot/image paths outside canonical evidence locations, or above the evidence size thresholds, unless a per-file allowlist includes purpose + claim/issue + owner + source SHA + review expiry.
- SHA duplicate detection across images, reports, registries, upstream snapshots and OSMesa/dependency files. Duplicate SHA detection must distinguish a safe symlink/alias from duplicated regular files. Fail or warn on duplicate paths without documented reason.
- Ensure all generated documents/registries declare their source and generator; fail if two files claim to be the same authoritative registry.
- Catch absolute developer paths such as `/home/z/my-project`, `/home/z/...`, `C:\\Users\\...` and machine-specific output paths in committed scripts/reports, except explicitly marked historical records.
- Catch new per-run screenshot duplication and repeated screenshot embeddings in Markdown.
- Catch contradictory evidence: `NO_APP_OPS` with `REAL_APP_CONTENT`, zero app draw operations presented as complete UI, stale screenshot sizes, mismatched run/APK paths, SUCCESS that hides uncaught exceptions or stub-bounded behavior.
- Support narrow, source-reviewed exceptions. No blanket allowlist for a whole directory and no “ignore all PNG/JSON” bypass.
- Add positive tests to prove legitimate runtime sources, pinned source references, fixtures and canonical assets still pass; add negative tests for each forbidden artifact class.
- CI should run the validator, classifier tests and evidence validator on every PR. It must not download the complete Android toolchain merely to inspect repository paths.

## 7. Ownership and cleanup responsibility

- Each top-level directory has one owner (runtime, tests, docs, evidence, dependencies, tooling, or project governance).
- Each active evidence batch has one named maintainer/issue, a date and a retirement decision.
- Every temporary artifact is removed at run end; every promoted artifact has a reason to live.
- Once an issue/wave closes, its scratch area is frozen and reviewed. It does not become a general-purpose folder for future work.
- Every quarter/release, run a full tree scan and publish a compact hygiene delta. No automatic mass deletions; every removal gets a path/SHA/consumer/disposition record.
- This is a permanent project law and must be included verbatim or linked in all coder request templates, including Coder 2–9 and main-coder requests.

## 8. R26–R35 permanent acceptance items

- [ ] **R26 OSMESA PURPOSE:** all repository consumers identified; test-only/runtime role decided; exact duplicate ELF paths and package/extracted duplication resolved; clean optional test or removal proof attached.
- [ ] **R27 FORENSIC DATA:** all 237 inputs classified; patch parts resolved; unique audit facts retained; raw exports removed/externalized only after canonical ledger rebuild/validation.
- [ ] **R28 ROOT LAW:** root allowlist documented and all existing stray files moved/removed with provenance.
- [ ] **R29 DIRECTORY OWNERSHIP:** every top-level directory has exactly one owner and purpose; ambiguous/overlapping roots consolidated or explicitly retained.
- [ ] **R30 CONSTITUTION:** permanent chapter added to `CONSTITUTION_V2.md`; linked from contribution/agent guides; conflicting old policies reconciled.
- [ ] **R31 FILE CONTRACT:** every new tracked file uses the pre-write classification/consumer/provenance/lifecycle contract.
- [ ] **R32 CI ENFORCEMENT:** root/directory/artifact/duplicate/absolute-path/evidence contradiction checks are automatic and tested.
- [ ] **R33 NO-REGRESSION:** running clean builds/tests leaves no untracked or newly tracked residue in the source tree.
- [ ] **R34 CODER ALIGNMENT:** main coder + Coders 2–9 request templates explicitly require Constitution compliance; no lane may create its own top-level folder or artifact dump.
- [ ] **R35 FINAL MAP:** publish `docs/REPOSITORY_STRUCTURE.md` with every retained top-level directory, owner, allowed classes, forbidden classes, canonical links and migration status.

**Completion rule:** The Constitution chapter, ownership map, executable validator, tests and CI must land together. A policy paragraph without a failing CI test is not an enforced law. Do not close #587 or #386 based only on documentation; prove the next deliberately misplaced file is rejected and a legitimate source/fixture/evidence file passes.
